name: BGD-TCCF Plastics Circularity
description: Plastics have become an integral part of daily life, used for items such as straws, shopping bags, electronics, and construction materials. The prevailing linear model of take, make, use, and dispose results in significant plastic waste accumulation, with forecasts suggesting 12 billion tons of plastic will be in landfills and the environment by 2050. Globally, the environmental, climate, and health impacts of plastics are nearing US$139 billion annually, adversely affecting freshwater systems, marine resources, terrestrial biodiversity, and public health. Adopting a circular economy would mitigate plastic production, use, and disposal.Urbanization and development have escalated plastic consumption and waste, often leading to clogging of rivers and water bodies. Plastics break down into harmful microplastics, posing risks to both humans and ecosystems. In Bangladesh, annual per capita plastic consumption in urban areas has significantly increased, with single-use plastic bags and multilayer plastics being major contributors to landfill waste. Addressing the challenges associated with plastics requires a life-cycle approach, including bans, recycling, and alternative materials. Nonetheless, without a comprehensive, multistakeholder plan grounded in circular economy principles, effectively tackling plastic issues remains challenging. Greater industry involvement, inter-ministry coordination, and attention to the informal sectors role are essential for creating a sustainable action plan.Implementing a market-driven decentralized circular economy model for plastic waste management in Chattogram, Cox’s Bazar, and Tangail aims to preserve the value of plastics in the economy while protecting the natural environment. This initiative includes policy advocacy and awareness efforts targeting government agencies, the private sector, city authorities, and local communities to foster a collaborative approach to waste management.

name: Sustainable solutions to plastic pollution in Senegal
description: Ce projet financé par le GEF (Subvention : 5 048 777 USD ; Co-financement : 41 280 466 USD) vise à réduire lutilisation et lélimination des emballages en plastique à usage unique dans les secteurs de lalimentation et des boissons au Sénégal. Le principal défi de développement abordé par le projet est limpératif de solutions circulaires à la pollution plastique, visant à accélérer la transition vers une économie circulaire pour les plastiques. Pour atteindre cet objectif, le projet développera des incitations pour lutilisation sûre, efficace et circulaire des plastiques. De plus, il facilitera des mécanismes financiers et un soutien pour le développement de startups et de recherches universitaires axées sur linnovation et des solutions alternatives aux produits en plastique.Le projet se concentrera sur des interventions en amont et en milieu de chaîne pour éliminer les produits en plastique inutiles et problématiques, ainsi que les plastiques contenant des additifs dangereux. Le projet comporte quatre composantes :1.Renforcement de la capacité du gouvernement à mettre en oeuvre le cadre juridique existant (cadres juridique, institutionnel et de coordination)2.Changement de comportement, sensibilisation et gestion des connaissances.3.Engagement du secteur privé et mobilisation des financements.4.Suivi, évaluation, rapport et coordination au niveau du programme.Le projet fournira des Bénéfices Environnementaux Globaux (BEGs) en évitant 33 000 MTCO2, en réduisant 9 000 tonnes de déchets toxiques, en réduisant 20 g TEQ, et en bénéficiant à des femmes (2 041 255) et des hommes (2 102 802), pour un total de 4 144 056 bénéficiaires

Target provinces include Phnom Penh, Siem Reap, and Preah Sihanouk for interventions in the hospitality, tourism, and F&B sectors. The project will attain the following four (4) project components: ? name: PPG: Transforming Nauru’s Food Systems through Climate Smart Agriculture
description: The objective of the GEF PPG is to develop the project concept into a full project: “Transforming Nauru’s Food Systems through Climate Smart Agriculture”. As described in the child project concept note of the Food Systems Integrated Program (FSIP), this project aims to implement Nauru’s Climate Smart Agriculture Plan (NaCSAP) to contribute to food and nutrition security. NaCSAP is a holistic, island-wide approach that is vertically integrated and coordinated through a whole-of-government platform. There is also integration of national priorities such as reducing import dependency/ increasing food and nutrition security and addressing sustainable development, environmental conservation related commitments, and the SDGs.The project is designed to showcase sustainable food production systems within the context of Small Island Developing States (SIDS) to achieve food security, enhance nutrition diversity, and improve health and well-being while simultaneously protecting critical ecosystems, including coastal, marine, and vital freshwater resources. It aims to assist Nauru in incorporating nature-smart and climate-resilient food production solutions into the NaSCAP. These solutions are nature-smart by conserving freshwater, preventing coastal and marine pollution, managing plastic waste from tunnel agriculture, minimizing chemical inputs, and addressing invasive species management—a prevalent issue in the Pacific. Additionally, the project will employ innovative technologies to conserve land, water, and coastal areas. The climate-resilient aspects include water conservation measures, the utilization of weather-proof greenhouses, and the reduction of greenhouse gases (GHG) using renewable energy sources for cooling systems and fertilizer conveyance.
focusArea: Leaving no one behind

name: Plastic Waste Management: Towards a New Social Contract in Partnership with the Private sector
description: The Republic of Djibouti faces major challenges in the collection, management, and treatment of waste—especially plastic waste—in both urban and rural areas. Municipalities are currently responsible for waste management, but they face significant obstacles: approximately 344 tons of waste are generated daily, of which 20% is plastic—a volume that continues to rise due to population growth and urbanization. This situation is further hampered by the lack of official, reliable, and accessible data, as well as limited coordination, which prevents the implementation of effective solutions. Additionally, Djiboutis private sector, still in its early stages of development, suffers from structural constraints, notably limited access to diversified financing mechanisms. Young entrepreneurs, micro-businesses, and SMEs struggle to mobilize the resources needed to develop innovative projects, particularly in waste management. The weakness of the private sector thus hinders the emergence of new and dynamic solutions, which are essential for a successful green transition.

name: Tanzania National Plastic Action Plan (TZ-NPAP)
description: The World Economic Forum (the “Forum”) is an independent international institution committed toimproving the state of the world by engaging business, political, academic and other leaders of society toshape global, regional and industry agendas. The Forum, incorporated as a foundation in 1971 and basedin Geneva, Switzerland, is impartial, not-for-profit and is tied to no political, partisan or national interests. The Global Plastic Action Partnership (GPAP) hosted by the Forum was launched in September 2018 atthe Sustainable Development Investment Summit as a lighthouse initiative within the Platform for Shapingthe Future of Global Public Goods. GPAP is a public-private platform which aims to tackle one of the mostdifficult and pressing challenges facing our global commons — plastics pollution — in particular the plasticpollution of rivers, deltas and the ocean. The vision of GPAP is to partner with countries to champion a shift towards a circular plastics economy byaddressing the root causes of plastic pollution, from production to consumption and reuse. GPAP bringstogether governments, regional bodies, international organizations and businesses, as well as innovatorsand civil society organizations on an impartial collaboration platform with the aim to shape a moresustainable and inclusive world through the eradication of plastic pollution. At the global level as well asnationally through National Plastic Action Partnerships (NPAPs), the GPAP brings together policymakers,business leaders and civil society to accelerate plastic action in six ways: informing policy; unlockingfinance; transforming behaviour; boosting innovation; harmonizing metrics; and promoting inclusivity.

name: National Plastic Action Partnership in the Philippines
description: Plastic pollution is recognized as a symptom of deeper systemic issues, including unsustainable production and consumption patterns, inadequate waste management infrastructure, legal frameworks, and enforcement, as well as economic, behavioral, and political factors. There is a pressing need for holistic solutions that address these root causes comprehensively.The National Plastic Action Partnership (NPAP) is a collaborative initiative spearheaded by the World Economic Forum (WEF) and the Global Plastic Action Partnership (GPAP). Its aim is to tackle the global challenge of plastic pollution by bringing together stakeholders from various sectors to develop and implement strategies that reduce plastic pollution and transition towards a circular economy. This can be achieved through 1) establishing organizational and operation procedures of NPAP and developing stakeholder engagement mechanism, 2) generate evidences from studies that feed into national action roadmap and community engagement, and 3) strengthening coordination and collaborations for initiatives on plastic action.UNDP Philippines will act as the NPAP Secretariat for the Philippines. The NPAP Secretariat in the Philippines will play a critical role in coordinating and implementing the NPAPs initiatives in the country.
focusArea: Structural transformation, including green, inclusive and digital transitions

name: Circular Economy for the Recovery of Waste Transition
description: The Circular Economy for the Recovery of Waste Transition (CERO Waste Transition) builds on and intends to further the successes of the pilot phase to consolidate a foundation for a scalable transition to an inclusive and climate-resilient circular economy (CE), targeting the plastic waste stream, that accounts for Samoa’s second largest waste stream and a problematic source of terrestrial and marine ecosystem pollution and degradation. As plastic waste pollution and its associated environmental impacts are exacerbated by multiple factors, a holistic approach is proposed that integrates convening power, systems thinking, institutional capacity building, education and awareness-building, technological innovation and on-the-ground action to accelerate the transition to a CE, leveraging actors from across the public, private and civil society sector due to the multi-stakeholder nature of the issue.
focusArea: Structural transformation, including green, inclusive and digital transitions

name: National Plastic Action Partnership in Lao PDR
description: Plastic pollution is recognized as a symptom of deeper systemic issues, including unsustainable production and consumption patterns, inadequate waste management infrastructure, legal frameworks, and enforcement, as well as economic, behavioral, and political factors. There is a pressing need for holistic solutions that address these root causes comprehensively.UNDP Lao PDR will act as the NPAP Secretariat for Lao PDR. The NPAP Secretariat in Lao PDR will play a critical role in coordinating and implementing the NPAPs initiatives in the country.
focusArea: Building resilience

name: Global Plastics Offer (GPO) – Support the Start-up Phase (Engagement Facility)
description: UNDP entered into a global partnership with the Ocean Cleanup in support of the implementation of UNDP’s Plastics Offer. The goal of the partnership is to jointly develop solutions for the reduction of leakages of plastics into marine ecosystems from rivers, basins and terrestrial and marine resources through deployment of technologies, policy advocacy and behavior change. This global partnership builds on the experiences and lessons learned from the national level cooperation between UNDP-Dominican Republic and the Ocean Cleanup. Eight priority countries have been identified for this partnership considering various factors including pollution status, existing relationship, and past/ongoing plastic work. The 8 countries are Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, India, Dominican Republic, Guatemala, and Jamaica.
focusArea: Structural transformation, including green, inclusive and digital transitions

name: Reduction of POPs & U-POPs
description: The project intends to ensure integrated solid waste management towards zero waste and a circular economy vision for Eswatini. The main focus of the waste streams in this project includes healthcare waste, e-waste, and plastic waste. The project will help reduce pollution from chemicals and waste, improve the health and livelihoods of the general population and workers through a gender-responsive approach, and foster green growth through public and private partnerships in the services of waste management and circular businesses, particularly SMEs.
focusArea: Structural transformation, including green, inclusive and digital transitions

name: Circular Solution to Plastic Pollution
description: to promote Jordan transition to circular economy model with focus on plastic waste
focusArea: Structural transformation, including green, inclusive and digital transitions

name: Circular solutions to plastic pollution in Morocco
description: The aim of the GEF-funded project “Circular Solutions to Plastics Morocco” (SAP ID 230062) is to hasten the shift toward a circular economy for plastics within Moroccos food and beverage industry, by advancing circular practices and supporting Morocco’s National Strategy to Sustainable Development.In line with GEF terminology, UNIDO is the GEF Implementing Agency (IA) for the Project and Ministry of Energetic Transition and Sustainable Development - Department of Sustainable Development (MTEDD) will act as national lead agency. Project execution will be undertaken by UNDP Morocco Country Office.
focusArea: Structural transformation, including green, inclusive and digital transitions

name: Integrated Environmental Management and Climate Resilience Programme (IEMCRP)
description: The Gambia faces mounting environmental and climate challenges, including deforestation, land degradation, biodiversity loss, and coastal erosion. Rising temperatures and erratic rainfall patterns are disrupting agriculture, tourism, fisheries, and public health. Coastal communities are increasingly vulnerable to floods and sea-level rise, highlighting the need for robust disaster risk mitigation.Municipal solid waste generation exceeds 530 tons daily, projected to reach over 1,000 tons by 2030, with plastic pollution rising sharply. Infrastructure for chemical and hazardous waste management remains limited, posing risks to ecosystems and human health The country’s Blue Economy—anchored in its coastline and river systems—offers sustainable growth in fisheries, tourism, maritime transport, and renewable energy. However, overexploitation and pollution threaten its long-term viability. Biodiversity management is critical to restoring degraded habitats and enhancing ecosystem resilience.Aligned with its Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC2), The Gambia aims to reduce emissions by 49.7% by 2030. This project supports national goals by promoting clean energy and clean cooking solutions, strengthening natural resource and biodiversity management, and advancing gender-responsive economic empowerment through targeted training.Under UNDP’s Environment and Climate Resilience pillar, strategic interventions will focus on climate and disaster risk management, sustainable energy access, solid and chemical waste management, biodiversity conservation, and inclusive livelihoods.
focusArea: Structural transformation, including green, inclusive and digital transitions

name: Plastic waste management at the local level
description: The project objective is to minimize negative impacts and risks to environment and to human health through promoting sustainable plastic waste management practices at the local level.
focusArea: Accelerate structural transformations

name: UNCTAD UNDP WORKSHOP
description: Organization of a 3-day regional workshop in Suva, Fiji entitled: “Regional Indo-Pacific workshop on oceans economy, plastic pollution, and plastic substitutes” including related substantive and logistical elements. The workshop will assist countries in the Indo-pacific region to better understand material substitutes as part of solutions under SDG 14.1 and 12. The activity will also assist in building a stronger voice of Pacific Nations in multilateral processes on plastic pollution, including the WTO Dialogue on Plastic Pollution and the Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee towards a binding international instrument on plastic pollution.
focusArea: Structural transformation, including green, inclusive and digital transitions

name: Nudging the Private Sector to Address Waste Management
description: This initiative is to address waste management through behavioral insights and also engage with the private sector
